root_idea.summary: The root centers on a clear or open path and the making of something manifest, alongside a distinct lexical branch involving interrupted breath, fatigue, and wearing out.
root_idea.development: The path-and-clarity branch yields nouns for a clear road or way and verbs meaning to become or make manifest. Classical evidence also preserves a separate branch of panting or becoming breathless, falling from beating, and garment wear.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Display as the normalized dictionary citation form مِنْهَاج rather than the Quranic accusative surface form مِنْهَاجًا.

senses.definition: A clear, plainly apparent way or path.
senses.usage_conditions: In the supplied Quran occurrence, the noun is paired with شِرْعَةً in the expression “a law and a clear way.” The evidence supports the lexical value of a clear way or path.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become manifest, plainly apparent, or open; to make a road, way, or affair manifest or clear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The intransitive use describes something becoming clear or open; the transitive or causative use describes making it clear, including a road, way, or affair.
Used with a road or way as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a garment, to become old and worn out without being torn into several pieces; to wear a garment out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The intransitive forms describe a garment becoming worn from attrition; the causative use describes wearing it out or the effect of wear spreading through it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become out of breath, breathe short, or pant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The use describes breathlessness or panting resulting from violent motion or exertion and is attested of persons and animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To beat someone until he fell or lay stretched out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a resultative construction describing the outcome of severe beating.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause a person or riding animal to pant and become fatigued or jaded.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form IV causative describes inducing breathlessness and exhaustion, including by riding an animal hard.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To follow another person’s way or path.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction is attested with سبيل or طريق followed by the person whose way is taken.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Causative clarity use covered by the same meaning.
Illustrative example of the clarity construction.
Garment becoming or being made worn out.

Beating until falling or becoming stretched out.
Clear or manifest road and way.
Plain or open track of a road.
Pointer-only cross-reference identifying مِنْهَاج through نَهْج.

cautions: The supplied Quran evidence attests مِنْهَاج only as a noun in one occurrence; the Form I, Form IV, and Form X verbal branches are supported here as broader Classical Arabic meanings.

One Form IV passage records an alternative reading of the result of beating as “wept,” but the same passage flags that reading as likely erroneous; the supported sense is falling or becoming stretched out.
